dedupe_keys.name: doe national transmission needs study draft of july 2026

description: The National Transmission Needs Study is the Department of Energy's triennial assessment of national electric transmission capacity constraints and congestion, required by Congress, and this page presents the draft released on 9 July 2026 for public comment until 8 September 2026. The Grid Deployment Office prepared it from publicly available information and more than 120 recently published reports on historic and anticipated needs under a range of demand, policy and market conditions; since 2023 the scope covers future as well as historic constraints. Its key findings are a pressing need for more transmission driven by load growth including hyperscale data centres and electrification, congestion concentrated in about 5 percent of hours, the highest potential for new within-region lines in NYISO, NorthernGrid South and MISO, and high congestion value in interregional links using historical locational marginal prices. Coverage is the United States. Access: the draft report, supplemental methodology and data, an informational webinar and FAQs, all free on the page; no licence is stated. Caveats: a draft that may change, an assessment of needs and not a set of transmission solutions, and it does not replace regional planning. It suits capacity planning and investment appraisal inputs and relates to the EIA-930 hourly grid monitor catalogued here.
